ChannelListRules.description: What a channel list parameter accepts beyond the default, per the manual (#260).

descending.description: A descending range (@2:1) is accepted and expands in its written order (2, 1), as the B2900 manual lists; false: -222
descending.title: Descending

empty.description: An empty list (@) is accepted, e.g. the DAQ970A's ROUT:SCAN (@) clearing the scan list (#418); false: -108
empty.title: Empty

repeated.description: A channel may appear more than once, answered each time; false: -108
repeated.title: Repeated

ChannelListRules.title: ChannelListRules

ChannelNumbering.description: One block of channel numbers: ``first`` .. ``first + count - 1``, numbers SCPI uses.

count.description: How many channels the block has, e.g. 20
count.title: Count

first.description: The block's first channel number, e.g. 101
first.title: First

ChannelNumbering.title: ChannelNumbering

lists.description: Channel list parameters (@…): whether descending ranges, repeated channels and an empty list are accepted (#260, #418)

numbering.description: The numbers SCPI uses for the channels, when they are not 1..count: blocks in channel order, e.g. a 3-slot DAQ's 101-120, 201-220, 301-320. State paths and channels.overrides keep the channel index (1..count).
numbering.title: Numbering

overrides.description: Per-channel overrides of channel_state specs, e.g. {3: {frequency: {max: 2e8}}}
overrides.title: Overrides

selected.description: An int setting holding the selected output's channel number (INSTrument:SELect / NSELect, #295): a channel list parameter left out uses it instead of the parameter's default
selected.title: Selected

CommandSpec.description:
One SCPI command: bound to a setting (``state``), to a component operation (``op``), or, through
its parameters' ``state``, to several settings at once.

args.description: Constant arguments passed to the operation
args.title: Args

factor.description: The command's number is the bound setting times factor: :TIMebase:RANGe is factor 10 on the time/div setting; a write divides by it
factor.title: Factor

read.description: An operation command's query reads this setting instead of calling the operation: 'OPER' enters operate, 'OPER?' reads it (the setting the operation writes)
read.title: Read

reply.description: Query reply template: {header} (the echoed header, see dialect.echo_header; with echo off it and the space after it are left out), {value} (the bound setting, or an operation's reply), {value_block} (that reply as an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block, e.g. '#13(@)') and {<setting>}, e.g. '{header} {value} V'. Default: '{header} {value}' for settings; an operation's reply as it is
reply.title: Reply

set_value.description: A setting command without parameters writes this constant and its query reads it back (LOCAL / REMOTE / LOCKOUT, which only set the interface state)
set_value.title: Set Value

state.description: State path bound to the command, e.g. 'ch.frequency'
state.title: State

when.description: Use this command only when parameters have these values, e.g. {name: DATA_ARRAY_1}: several commands may share a header, told apart by a parameter (C1:INSPECT? "WAVEDESC")
when.title: When

writes.description: Settings a multi-setting command writes along with its parameters, e.g. {sense.function: VOLT} for CONFigure:VOLTage:DC: the command header itself selects the function. Validated like a parameter and written before them (the parameters win). On an operation's command they are written before the operation runs (#308: MEASure:CURRent? selects the current function, as the instrument does)
writes.title: Writes

CommandSpec.title: CommandSpec

params.description: Parameter values: a literal, a setting ('$ch.frequency') or a mapping of a setting ({from, map, scale, offset, default})
params.title: Params

DeviationSpec.description: A definition's deviation: which component parameter, and its range.

by.description: Draw one value per cell of a table, e.g. {function: [DC], range: [0.1, 1, 10]}: the parameter becomes the nested table {DC: {0.1: …, 1: …, 10: …}}
by.title: By

coverage.description: normal: the coverage factor k of the limit (limit = k·σ)
coverage.title: Coverage

distribution.description: uniform: anywhere within ±limit; normal: σ = limit / coverage, truncated at ±limit (a unit outside its specification is a fault, injected separately)
distribution.title: Distribution

limit.description: ±limit. A number, or with `by` a table keyed by the values of the last `by` key (e.g. {0.1: 30, 1: 20} per range)
limit.title: Limit

param.description: '<component>.<parameter>', e.g. 'meter.gain_error_ppm'; a channel component's name (e.g. 'out.z_out') draws one value per channel
param.title: Param

unit.description: '%' or 'ppm': relative to the nominal value, value = nominal × (1 + d). Omitted: the limit is in the parameter's own unit, value = nominal + d (a parameter that is itself an error, e.g. gain_error_ppm, or an offset)
unit.title: Unit

DeviationSpec.title: DeviationSpec

Dialect.description:
How replies are framed, for instruments that are not plain SCPI (e.g. LeCroy's ``C1:VDIV 200E-3 V``).

The defaults are SCPI: no header in replies, numbers without multiplier suffixes.

echo_header.description: Replies start with the command header: off, short (C1:VDIV), long (C1:VOLT_DIV), or a setting whose value is OFF, SHORT or LONG ('$comm.header', switched by COMM_HEADER)
echo_header.title: Echo Header

multipliers.description: Suffixes of numbers written without a unit, e.g. {K: 1.0e3, M: 1.0e6} for 'MSIZ 10K'
multipliers.title: Multipliers

Dialect.title: Dialect

actions.description: Front-panel buttons as the model's own commands, run inside the instrument (not over SCPI, D32), e.g. {single: ':TRIGger:MODE SINGle'}; run, stop and single default to the acquisition component's operations
actions.title: Actions

panel.description: Front-panel layout: readings on the main display, grouped controls, softkeys (instrument-authoring.md 7.3)

Panel.description:
The instrument's front panel as the UI draws it (instrument-authoring.md 7.3): the main
display's readings, groups of controls, and softkeys. Without one, a multimeter and a calibrator
get their class's default layout; the classes with a dedicated screen do not use it.
Panel.title: Panel

PanelControl.description: One setting on the panel, and the control it is set with (instrument-authoring.md 7.3).

control.description: buttons: a key per value (an enum's options, or `keys`); number: a value with its unit and step keys; switch: on / off (bool); select: a drop-down (enum)
control.title: Control

keys.description: buttons: the keys; default for an enum: one per option, for a bool: on and off
keys.title: Keys

step.description: number: what the step keys add and subtract
step.title: Step

unit.description: number: the unit shown; default: the setting's
unit.title: Unit

PanelControl.title: PanelControl

label.description: The group's title, e.g. 测量, 量程, 触发
label.title: Label

PanelKey.description: One key of a button group: the value it writes, and what it reads on the instrument.

label.description: The key's text; default: the option's label or the value
label.title: Label

sets.description: Further settings written along with it, e.g. {sense.range_auto: false} for a range key; the key is lit while all of them hold
sets.title: Sets

value.description: The value the key writes to the control's setting
value.title: Value

PanelKey.title: PanelKey

PanelReadout.description: A reading on the main display.

reading.description: A reading of the instrument, '<component>.<reading>', e.g. 'meter.DC'
reading.title: Reading

unit.description: The reading's unit, e.g. V; none for a count or a word
unit.title: Unit

when.description: Shown only while these settings have these values, e.g. {sense.function: VOLT}
when.title: When

PanelReadout.title: PanelReadout

PanelSoftkey.description: A key under the display: a front-panel action (D32), or a setting written to a value.

action.description: A front-panel action, as `display.actions` names them
action.title: Action

sets.description: Further settings written along with it
sets.title: Sets

PanelSoftkey.title: PanelSoftkey

ParamSpec.description: A parameter of an operation command.

combine.description: type quantities: what a combination of units writes besides, keyed by the units joined with commas in the `units` table's order ('V,HZ'); a value may be conditional, {if_zero: <state>, then: ..., else: ...}. A combination not listed is refused
combine.title: Combine

combine_error.description: Error code for a combination of units `combine` does not list
combine_error.title: Combine Error

default.description: type channel_list: the channels used when the optional parameter is omitted, e.g. [1] for an instrument whose (@1) may be left out
default.title: Default

duplicate_unit_error.description: Error code for a unit given twice in one command
duplicate_unit_error.title: Duplicate Unit Error

echo.description: Whether a query's answer repeats this index first (PACU? 1 -> 1,AMPL,C1); false for instruments that answer only the settings (SR830 DDEF? 1 -> j,k, #273)
echo.title: Echo

index.description: An int that picks which settings the other parameters write: their state paths name it in braces, e.g. 'measure.p{slot}.kind' (PACU 1,AMPL,C1); a query takes it too (PACU? 1). A set takes it at its own position (VIEW CHAN2; TRIG:LEV 0.5,CHAN2); a query takes the index parameters alone, in order
index.title: Index

index_default.description: An optional index's value when it is left out: a number, or a $setting whose value (an index word or a number) picks it, e.g. $trigger.source for :TRIG:LEV <level>[,<source>]
index_default.title: Index Default

index_numbers.description: With index_words: the number may be written instead of the word (SR86x CDSP 0 = CDSP DAT1, #333); a number that is not one of the words' numbers is -222
index_numbers.title: Index Numbers

index_words.description: An index written as a word (#248): the word's number, e.g. {CHANnel1: 1, CHANnel2: 2} for :VIEW CHANnel2; the query answer echoes the word's short form
index_words.title: Index Words

keys.description: type pairs: 'name,value,name,value...'; each name writes the setting it maps to, null accepts the name and ignores its value. All values are checked before any is set
keys.title: Keys

keywords.description: Settings a keyword argument writes in place of the parameter's own value, keyed by MIN, MAX, DEF or a special word, e.g. {MIN: {sense.nplc: 100, sense.resolution: 0}} for a resolution argument whose MIN selects the finest integration time; the parameter's own setting is written only when the table names it
keywords.title: Keywords

missing_unit_error.description: Error code for a value without a unit (the text comes from `errors`)
missing_unit_error.title: Missing Unit Error

not_modeled.description: Words the real instrument takes for this parameter but the model does not implement, with the reason (as on a setting, #360); refused with -224 as not modeled
not_modeled.title: Not Modeled

sets.description: Settings this parameter writes along with its own when it is given, e.g. {sense.range_auto: false} for a range argument that leaves autorange; not written when the argument is DEF or a special word of the setting (AUTO)
sets.title: Sets

state.description: Setting this parameter writes (a command without `state` or `op`); it is parsed as that setting reads values
state.title: State

units.description: type quantities: comma-separated 'value unit' parameters, each written into the setting its unit names, e.g. {V: {state: out.level}, HZ: {state: out.frequency}}; the multiplier moves into the value (mV, kHz)
units.title: Units

unknown_unit_error.description: Error code for a unit the `units` table does not name
unknown_unit_error.title: Unknown Unit Error

ParamSpec.title: ParamSpec

media.description: What an exposed port carries when it is not plain electrical, e.g. {REF_IN: reference} for a timebase or lock-in reference; the canvas draws such wires as reference wires
media.title: Media

QuantityUnit.description:
What one unit of a ``quantities`` parameter means (metrology-authoring.md 5.2): the setting
the value writes, and further settings written at the same time.

sets.description: Further settings written along with it, e.g. {out.unit: V} or {out.function: DCI}
sets.title: Sets

state.description: The setting the value writes, e.g. 'out.level'
state.title: State

QuantityUnit.title: QuantityUnit

Reference.description:
The basis a definition follows (D42), provided and maintained by its author: a vendor manual,
the author's own design specification, or an interface contract. A definition with a reference
is a real model: unknown commands answer -113 and `unknown_commands: ignore` is refused.

document.description: Document or part number; an internal specification's identifier
document.title: Document

title.description: e.g. 'Keysight Truevolt Series Operating and Service Guide' or 'XX 型 SCPI 接口规格 草案 v0.3'
title.title: Title

version.description: Edition, revision or date of the basis
version.title: Version

Reference.title: Reference

ResponseFormat.description:
How query responses are written (real models, D42): numbers, booleans and enumerations.

The defaults are what ``sb-*`` instruments have always returned, e.g. ``+1.000000E+03``.

digits.description: Digits after the decimal point (nr3 mantissa, nr2); significant digits (general)
digits.title: Digits

enum.description: short: SIN; long: SINUSOID (upper case); as_defined: SINusoid, as in `options`
enum.title: Enum

error_code.description: Code in :SYSTem:ERRor? replies: plain: 0,"No error"; signed: +0,"No error"
error_code.title: Error Code

exponent_digits.description: nr3: digits of the exponent, e.g. E+03 is 2
exponent_digits.title: Exponent Digits

number.description: nr3: +1.000000E+03; nr2: +1000.000000; nr1: +1000 (rounded); engineering: 1E+3, 200E-3 (exponent a multiple of 3, shortest mantissa); si: 4.00000000MHz — `significant` digits with an SI prefix and `unit` (#289); general: C %g with `digits` significant digits, lowercase e and no trailing zeros, 2.3346669042e-09, 19.749698639 (#383)
number.title: Number

readings.description: Numbers a component answers (marker values, trace points, counter readings): component — each component's own digits (the default, what sb-* instruments return); format — written in this format like the settings, for a manual whose replies share one format (N9320B: 16 digits, #366). Components whose digits are a definition parameter (a meter's or trigger model's `digits`) keep that parameter
readings.title: Readings

significant.description: engineering with this many significant digits, signed and with exponent_digits: +40.0E+00 (3), +0.00000E+00 (6); a command's own format may set its own
significant.title: Significant

unit.description: number: si — the unit written after the prefix, e.g. Hz (default: the setting's)
unit.title: Unit

ResponseFormat.title: ResponseFormat

display_unit.description: Unit shown in the UI when it differs from `unit`, e.g. '×'
display_unit.title: Display Unit

electrical.description: Changing this variable changes the bench's circuit
electrical.title: Electrical

ladder.description: Snap writes to a ladder: '1-2-5', '1-3' or an explicit list of values
ladder.title: Ladder

not_modeled.description: Words the real instrument takes for this setting but the model does not implement, with the reason, e.g. {INFinity: continuous scanning is not modeled} (SCPI mixed case: the short and the long form both match). Writing one is refused with -224 as not modeled, instead of being parsed as a number and rejected as out of range (#360)
not_modeled.title: Not Modeled

option_labels.description: How the UI shows enum options, e.g. {ONEMeg: '1 MΩ', FIFTy: '50 Ω'}
option_labels.title: Option Labels

options.description: Enum options in SCPI mixed case, e.g. SINusoid
options.title: Options

replies.description: Enum: the word a query answers for an option, when the instrument answers with a different word than the one it accepts, e.g. {CURRent: CC} for a load whose :FUNC CURR reads back CC (#268); options not listed answer as usual
replies.title: Replies

special.description: Extra keywords accepted for numbers, e.g. {INF: .inf} for a high-Z load
special.title: Special

unit.description: Base SCPI unit for suffix parsing, e.g. HZ, V, S, OHM
unit.title: Unit

TemplateSource.description:
The template a definition was expanded from and the inputs it was given (instrument-authoring.md
7.4, D3). A record only: loading and running ignore it; expanding the inputs again reproduces the
definition as the template generated it.

inputs.description: The inputs, in the template's data-sheet language
inputs.title: Inputs

version.description: Template version the inputs were expanded with
version.title: Version

TemplateSource.title: TemplateSource

instrument.description: Signal wires at instrument level; '{n}' expands per channel
instrument.title: Instrument

builtins.description: Built-in headers this model answers (e.g. ['*IDN', '*OPC', '*RST']); the others are not modeled. Default: all of them
builtins.title: Builtins

deviations.description: Parameters a unit deviates in, and their ranges: a bench instance with deviation: from_specs draws its own values from the bench seed (个体偏差, metrology-authoring.md 7)
deviations.title: Deviations

error_queue.description: Error queue length; on overflow the last entry becomes -350 (SCPI-99 21.8)
error_queue.title: Error Queue

errors.description: Error texts by code: overrides standard texts and adds device-specific codes
errors.title: Errors

reference.description: The manual this definition follows; a definition with a reference is a real model: unknown commands answer -113 'not implemented in this definition', error texts follow `errors`

specs.description: Accuracy and other specifications from the manual, as written there; a record, not used in calculations (the deviations a unit draws are in `deviations`)
specs.title: Specs

template.description: The template and inputs this definition was expanded from (a record; not used when loading or running)

unknown_commands.description: A header the definition does not have: 'error' queues -113; 'ignore' swallows it (no error, no reply) and logs an 'ignored' event. Only for definitions without `reference` (D42)
unknown_commands.title: Unknown Commands
